newsitem.title: MONGOLIA: MMC in Mongolia power talks - officials.
newsitem.headline: MMC in Mongolia power talks - officials.

text.p: Malaysia Mining Corp Bhd (MMC) has begun talks with the Mongolian government to build a $285 million hydroelectric power plant in the north of the country, a senior government official said this week.

The plant on the Egiin river would be linked io Mongolia's currently inadequate power grid, the Central Energy System (CES), that covers the more industrialised northern and central provinces, including the capital Ulan Bator.

The Mongolian government would request a $20 million loan from the Asian Development Bank, while MMC would provide financing for the remaining $265 million, L. Yondongombo, chief of the energy department under the Ministry of Infrastructure Development, said in an interview.

MMC was seeking $50 million from the Asian Development Fund, $50 million from the Japanese Oil Service Corporation, and $50 million from other international organisations, he said. The rest would be direct investment by MMC.

Yondongombo said it was too early to comment on details of the equity breakdown and the construction schedule because these were still under discussion. However, the possibility of exporting power to neighbouring countries had been discussed, he said.
Mongolia's CES grid is now supported by five coal-burning plants in Mongolia and is connected to the Russian grid to import electricity at peak consumption times.
The grid needs power from a hydroelectric plant to ensure sustained supplies following increasingly frequent breakdowns among Mongolia's ageing Russian-built thermal plants, officials have said.
